headline: Approved previous minutes and discussed Friends of Winooski Library fundraising and the temporary library space.
summary: Library Committee members presented on their work, including fundraising by the Friends of Winooski Library, which has raised about $4,000 and has 56 members. Discussion covered attracting patrons to the temporary library space, which is expected to last about two years. The only recorded vote approved the prior meeting minutes.
decisions: Approved the minutes from the 8/12/26 meeting, unanimously.

decision_evidence.quote: SHCP Minutes from 8/12/26 moved by: Dana Howe and Second by: Courtney Blasius. Unanimously approved.

plain_text:
10/20/2026 - Minutes
Call to Order
Meeting convened at: 5:40 by acting Chair – Dana
SCHP Commissioners: Meredith Bushey, Carly Schneider, Dana Howe, and Courtney Blasius
Library Committee Members: Dana Visser, Prudence Doherty, Jess Wignall, Lauren Read, and 
Amanda Goldstein
City Staff present: Nate Eddy
City Council Liaison present: Deputy Mayor Bryn Oakleaf
Public Comment
No one present from public for comment
Approve Previous Meeting Minutes
SHCP Minutes from 8/12/26 moved by: Dana Howe and Second by: Courtney Blasius.
Unanimously approved.
Presentation from Winooski Memorial Library Committee
Introductions of SCHP and Library Committee members present
l Presentation & Discussion from Library Committee -
¡ Nate walked through Library ppt 
slides: https://www.winooskivt.gov/AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Item/13635?
fileID=19384
¡ Committee Work includes: 
n Long range planning 
n Advocacy for funding 
n Help with policy drafting, review of updates 
n Table at community events
¡ Group discussed the reason why they’re called a “Committee” rather than a 
“Commission.” The Committee was formed in the 1940s, and Commissions 
were established with the most recent City Master Plan (soon to be updated 
and adopted as the City’s Comprehensive Plan). 
¡ Nate emphasized revitalization of Friends of Winooski Library. He 
reviewedtheir 501(c)3 status and ability to fundraise on behalf of the Library; 
events held and funds raised to date; and events scheduled in the near future. 
So far they’ve raised ~$4,000, and have 56 members. 
¡ The group discussed a number of challenges and opportunities with the long 
term (~2 years) temporary space, and methods to draw in the community city-
wide to utilize programs and services offered. Nate noted a fairly new audience 
in the new space, and the need to draw in regulars from the previous spot as 
well as retain the newer patrons when they move back. 
¡ Many folks noted how bright and inviting the temp space is, and look forward 
to the renovations at the O’Brien Community Center achieving a similar vibe
Inclusion and Belonging Commission Liaison Updates
No one present from I&B for updates. Meredith noted that we may have a new Ambassador 
assigned soon but we’re waiting on clarity from the City Clerk on that.
City Council and City Staff Liaison Updates
City Council Updates: Deputy Mayor Oakleaf noted her appointment to the School Merger Buddy 
group from Council. The first meeting of that group was held on 10/14/26 during regular School 
Board meeting time and location. Those meetings will be held monthly for the next 11 months. A 
summary of that kickoff meeting can be found here: 
https://www.winooskivt.gov/AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Item/13619?fileID=19366
City Updates: Nate promoted the Halloween in Winooski events coming up. The final Farmer’s 
Market of the season is this Sunday and will be Halloween themed, and then pumpkin carving is 
Tues-Thursday at the Senior Center with the annual pumpkin lighting event on 10/31/26 and 
again on 11/1/26.
Other Business
Deputy Mayor Oakleaf noted there will be some pre-reading ahead of the next SCHP 
Commission meeting in November. As the City works to update the Comprehensive Plan, City 
Council is also taking a look at Commission structure to see what’s working, where there’s 
room for improvement, and any suggested changes to structure to consider.
Adjourn
Moved by Dana Howe, and Second by Carly at 6:40 pm.
I.
II.
III.
IV.
V.
VI.
VII.
VIII.
DRAFT
